best_section.where: from the yellow ring south, against the tree line backing onto the rail corridor, before the grey-roofed house behind it comes closer

drivers.seclusion: Near the ring the kerb backs onto dense trees and the rail corridor rather than a house front; houses sit further south, screened by the same bush line but only 12-15m back.
drivers.access_and_room: Sealed, lit residential street with no driveways or crossings on this stretch; it narrows toward the tracks, so a van would likely need to reverse back out rather than turn.
drivers.traffic: Quiet dead-end residential street off the main grid, well away from through traffic.
drivers.convention: No cars are visibly parked along this kerb, and there's no obvious parking lane, so a van would stand out a little.

flags: Steep near the top: about 6% grade over the first 10m
Rail corridor close alongside — possible train noise
No parked cars seen on this kerb for cover
sun_shade: Dense tree canopy overhangs the kerb from the rail-corridor side (west), shading most of the stretch through the day; it opens up a little toward the southern end.
cannot_judge: Whether there's room to turn at the dead end or only to reverse out
Frequency/timing of trains on the adjacent line
reasons: Backs onto rail corridor and bush, not a house front
No parked cars along the kerb for cover
summary: Quiet dead-end kerb backing onto bush and a rail corridor, but no parked cars and a steepish top end.
